routes_page_meta_og_description: Report your marine animal sighting in the Baltic Sea. Support marine research with your observations.
routes_page_text_ostsee_tiere_meerestier: Baltic Sea Animals – Report marine animals
sighting_behavior_meta_helptext: Describe the animals’ behaviour – Tip: ‘Swimming in one direction’ = a steady course
sighting_behavior_meta_valuetext: Behavioural observations reveal stress levels and foraging patterns – crucial for protected area planning
sighting_behavior_test: Please enter a valid behaviour category.
sighting_behaviortext_max: The description must not exceed 255 characters.
sighting_behaviortext_meta_helptext: Describe the behaviour in your own words
sighting_behaviortext_meta_placeholder: e.g. play behaviour, hunting, mating, interaction with boats
sighting_behaviortext_meta_valuetext: Free text also captures behaviour for which there is no category in the drop-down list
sighting_boatdrive_meta_helptext: Which propulsion system was used during the sighting?
sighting_boatdrive_meta_valuetext: The propulsion type determines the underwater noise and, consequently, the extent to which animals are disturbed
sighting_boatdrive_required: Please select the boat propulsion system.
sighting_boatdrive_test: Please select a valid boat propulsion system.
sighting_boatdrivetext_max: The description must not exceed 255 characters.
sighting_boatdrivetext_meta_helptext: Innovative propulsion systems are of particular interest for noise studies
sighting_boatdrivetext_meta_valuetext: New propulsion technologies could revolutionise wildlife watching
sighting_boattype_max: The boat type must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_boattype_meta_placeholder: e.g. sailing boat, motor yacht, kayak, fishing boat
sighting_boattype_meta_valuetext: Sailing boats allow you to approach animals as quietly as possible – kayaks can reach the shallowest waters for unique sightings
sighting_city_max: The place of residence must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_deadcondition_meta_helptext: Description of the state of preservation
sighting_deadcondition_required: Please describe the condition of the dead animal.
sighting_deadphonecontact_meta_helptext: Has the Oceanographic Museum already been notified of the dead animal find?
sighting_deadphonecontact_meta_valuetext: Avoids duplicate reports and coordinates the recovery operation
sighting_deadsex_meta_valuetext: Sex ratio is important for population structure
sighting_deadsize_meta_valuetext: Body length helps to determine age
sighting_distance_meta_helptext: How far away were the animals? (Estimate)
sighting_distance_meta_valuetext: The shorter the distance, the more reliably the species and number can be determined – this information helps to assess the significance of observations
sighting_distance_test: Please select a valid distance category.
sighting_distance_test_2: Please select a valid distance category.
sighting_distribution_meta_helptext: How were the animals arranged spatially?
sighting_distribution_meta_valuetext: Group formations reveal family structures – mother-calf pairs swim close together, whilst males often swim alone
sighting_distributiontext_max: The description must not exceed 255 characters.
sighting_distributiontext_meta_helptext: Particular group formations provide insights into social behaviour
sighting_distributiontext_meta_placehold: e.g. V-formation, in a circle, along the coastline
sighting_distributiontext_meta_valuetext: Unusual formations could indicate hunting strategies or defensive behaviour
sighting_email_email: Please enter a valid email address.
sighting_email_max: The email address must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_email_meta_helptext: How can we get in touch with you?
sighting_email_meta_valuetext: For any enquiries and to confirm the sighting
sighting_entrychannel_meta_helptext: Through which channel was the sighting reported?
sighting_entrychannel_meta_valuetext: Specifies the source of the report for statistical analysis
sighting_entrychannel_test: Please select a valid reporting channel.
sighting_fax_max: The fax number must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_firstname_max: The first name must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_firstname_meta_helptext: How would you like us to address you?
sighting_firstname_meta_valuetext: To get in touch in person
sighting_hasposition_meta_helptext: Do you know the exact GPS coordinates, or do you have a photo with GPS data?
sighting_hasposition_meta_valuetext: If not, please describe the area
sighting_homeport_max: The home port must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_homeport_meta_valuetext: Home ports reveal regional observation networks – Baltic Sea Citizen Science
sighting_internalcomment_max: Internal comments must not exceed 1,000 characters.
sighting_isdead_label: Is this a dead animal find?
sighting_isdead_meta_helptext: Were they live animals or was it a dead animal find?
sighting_isdead_meta_valuetext: Dead animal finds provide important information about causes of death
sighting_juvenilecount_max: If the number is more than 15, please enter 15
sighting_juvenilecount_meta_helptext: Were there any young animals among them? Please enter the number.
sighting_juvenilecount_meta_valuetext: The proportion of young animals indicates the health of the population
sighting_juvenilecount_min: The number must be 0 or greater
sighting_juvenilecount_test: The number of young animals cannot exceed the total number of animals
sighting_lastname_max: The name must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_lastname_meta_valuetext: To ensure the report can be clearly identified
sighting_latitude_max: The latitude must be between -90° and 90°
sighting_latitude_meta_helptext: Northern position (N) – the more decimal places, the more accurate
sighting_latitude_meta_valuetext: GPS accuracy: 6 decimal places = 11 cm accuracy
sighting_latitude_min: The latitude must be between -90° and 90°
sighting_longitude_max: The longitude must be between -180° and 180°
sighting_longitude_meta_helptext: Eastern position (E) – the more decimal places, the more accurate
sighting_longitude_meta_valuetext: Your GPS coordinates will be compared with other sightings
sighting_longitude_min: The longitude must be between -180° and 180°
sighting_mediaconsent_meta_helptext: May we publish your recordings — for example, on the sightings map or in the Oceanographic Museum’s publicity materials?
sighting_mediaconsent_meta_valuetext: Without your consent, the recordings will be used solely for the purpose of verifying your report
sighting_mediafile_max: The path/name must not be longer than 255 characters.
sighting_mediafile_meta_helptext: Every photo is valuable – even blurry ones can help with identification
sighting_mediafile_meta_placeholder: e.g. 3 photos of a harbour porpoise pod, 1 video of a leaping whale
sighting_mediafile_meta_valuetext: Photographs allow species identification and behaviour to be verified at a later date – this significantly increases the value of your report
sighting_mediaupload_meta_helptext: Would you like to upload any photos or videos?
sighting_mediaupload_meta_valuetext: Media improve the quality of documentation
sighting_nameconsent_meta_helptext: I agree that my name (first name and surname) may be displayed publicly on the map.
sighting_nameconsent_meta_valuetext: Enables observers to be acknowledged on the sighting map
sighting_notes_meta_helptext: Is there anything else you’d like to add?
sighting_notes_meta_valuetext: The German Oceanographic Museum passes on the sighting data directly to the international bodies responsible for the protection of Baltic Sea harbour porpoises (HELCOM and ASCOBANS)
sighting_otherobservations_max: Other notable observations must not exceed 1,000 characters.
sighting_otherobservations_meta_helptext: Changes in behaviour reveal the impact of climate change on marine animals
sighting_otherobservations_meta_placehol: The effects of climate change, plastic pollution, other marine life...
sighting_otherobservations_meta_valuetex: Distinctive features of the habitat help to place sightings within their environmental context
sighting_persistentdataconsent_meta_help: I agree that my contact details will be permanently stored on this device so that they can be used automatically for future reports. Without this consent, the data will be deleted when the browser is closed.
sighting_persistentdataconsent_meta_valu: Enables automatic completion for future reports
sighting_phone_max: The telephone number must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_phone_meta_valuetext: For prompt clarification in the event of unclear information
sighting_privacyconsent_meta_helptext: I agree that my sighting details (date, location, species, number) may be displayed publicly on the map and analysed for scientific purposes. Any photographs I upload will be transmitted and used to verify the accuracy of my report; I will decide separately whether they are to be published. My contact details will only be used for follow-up enquiries. I confirm that the information I have provided is correct.
sighting_privacyconsent_meta_valuetext: Enables data processing for scientific purposes and public presentation
sighting_privacyconsent_required: You must agree to the data protection terms in order to report your sighting
sighting_reaction_max: The response must not exceed 1,000 characters.
sighting_reaction_meta_helptext: How did the animals react to your presence?
sighting_reaction_meta_placeholder: e.g. approached with curiosity, fled, ignored...
sighting_reaction_meta_valuetext: Reactions to boats indicate the level of disturbance – ‘flight’ suggests stress and influences the size of protected areas
sighting_seamark_max: The name of the nautical mark is too long (maximum 255 characters)
sighting_seamark_meta_helptext: This is no longer recorded in the reporting form — new reports describe the location in the field above. It remains editable for existing reports and the legacy interface.
sighting_seamark_meta_placeholder: e.g. Dahmeshöved Lighthouse, Buoy 14, approach buoy
sighting_seamark_meta_valuetext: Navigation marks help scientists verify the position and build confidence in the quality of the data
sighting_seastate_meta_helptext: What were the conditions on the sea’s surface like?
sighting_seastate_meta_valuetext: When the sea is rough, the area of the sea that observers can reliably scan shrinks by around a third (Baltic Sea SCANS 2023 survey) – which is why your report helps to put sighting figures into the right context
sighting_seastate_test: Please enter a valid sea state.
sighting_shipcount_label: Number of other vessels in the immediate vicinity
sighting_shipcount_max: The number of vessels must not exceed 15.
sighting_shipcount_meta_helptext: How many other boats were nearby?
sighting_shipcount_meta_valuetext: The number of nearby vessels helps to put the impact of underwater noise into perspective. Even ‘0 vessels’ is an important piece of information
sighting_shipcount_min: The number of vessels must be a positive number.
sighting_shipname_max: The ship’s name must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_shipname_meta_placeholder: e.g. MS Seelöwe, SY Nordwind, FFK Seeadler
sighting_shipname_meta_valuetext: Ship names enable long-term analysis – according to our sightings database, individual ships have been reporting sightings again and again for over 20 years
sighting_shipnameconsent_meta_helptext: I agree that the vessel’s name may be displayed publicly on the map.
sighting_shipnameconsent_meta_valuetext: Enables observers to be acknowledged on the sighting map
sighting_sightingdate_meta_helptext: On which day did the sighting take place?
sighting_sightingdate_test: The date is in the future – please correct it
sighting_sightingfrom_label: From where was the sighting made?
sighting_sightingfrom_meta_valuetext: Whether the observation was made from a boat or from land helps to determine which area was actually visible – this is important for assessing the report
sighting_sightingfrom_required: Please state from where the sighting was made.
sighting_sightingfromtext_max: The entry must not exceed 255 characters.
sighting_sightingfromtext_max_2: The entry must not exceed 255 characters.
sighting_sightingfromtext_meta_helptext: Please describe your location in more detail
sighting_sightingfromtext_meta_placehold: e.g. a bridge, a balcony, a beach...
sighting_sightingfromtext_required: Please state from where the sighting was made.
sighting_sightingtime_matches: Invalid time – please use the format 14:30
sighting_sightingtime_meta_valuetext: Time records help to identify the animals’ daily rhythms – even a rough estimate is useful
sighting_species_label: What species of animal did you see?
sighting_species_meta_helptext: If you are unsure, select ‘Unknown whale species’ or ‘Unknown seal species’ rather than guessing
sighting_species_meta_valuetext: Species identification helps with population monitoring
sighting_street_max: The street name must not be longer than 64 characters.
sighting_street_meta_valuetext: Enables observers to be assigned locally
sighting_totalcount_max: If there are more than 15 animals, please enter 15
sighting_totalcount_meta_valuetext: Group size is important for population analyses
sighting_totalcount_min_2: The number must not be negative
sighting_totalcount_required: How many animals did you see?
sighting_verified_meta_helptext: Has the sighting been verified by an administrator?
sighting_visibility_meta_valuetext: Visibility helps to determine which area was actually visible – even a rough estimate is helpful when analysing the data
sighting_visibility_test: Please enter a valid visibility category.
sighting_waterway_max: The location description is too long (maximum 255 characters)
sighting_waterway_meta_helptext: Body of water, fairway or nearby landmarks
sighting_waterway_meta_placeholder: e.g. the Bay of Kiel, the Fehmarn Belt, off the Dahmeshöved lighthouse
sighting_waterway_meta_valuetext: The names of water bodies and landmarks help to determine regional population distribution – even approximate details are scientifically valuable
sighting_waterway_required: Please describe the location or select a GPS position
sighting_weatherdata_meta_helptext: Weather data automatically retrieved from the Open-Meteo API
sighting_weatherdata_meta_valuetext: Supplements manual weather data with accurate API data
sighting_winddirection_meta_helptext: Which direction was the wind coming from?
sighting_winddirection_meta_valuetext: Wind affects sea state and visibility – your weather data completes the ecological picture
sighting_winddirection_oneof: Please enter a valid wind direction.
sighting_windforce_max: Please enter a valid wind force between 0 and 12.
sighting_windforce_meta_valuetext: When the wind is stronger, it is harder to spot animals surfacing amongst the waves – this helps to put sighting figures into perspective
sighting_windforce_min: Please enter a valid wind force between 0 and 12.
sighting_zipcode_max: The postcode must not be longer than 5 characters.
